unmapped_findings: The wrought (hot-rolled) sample is a calcium-treated, low-phosphorus (0.006% P) Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel; Table I row 1 (Si 1.01, C 0.89, Mn 30.20, P 0.006, S 0.001, Mo 0.31, Al 8.85 wt.%) is the closest listed chemistry, although the text cites the alloy nominally as 0.5Mo.
Tensile strength in the wrought alloy increased by 200 MPa with aging (b0040).

Fig. 7(b) indicates the wrought sample spans roughly 16–55% elongation with UTS from just below 1200 MPa down to between 900 and 1000 MPa as elongation increases (approximate values read from gridlines).

The fully austenitic microstructure and annealing-twin/equiaxed-grain refinement behavior of hot rolling are discussed generally in the introduction (b0007, figure_001), but the explicit 50 µm average grain size in figure_001 belongs to a different hot-rolled alloy (Fe-29Mn-6Al-0.9C-0.29Si-0.44Nb-0.44Mo), not this sample.
